item.title: Today in Motorsport History, November 6: Melandri Beat Hayden by 0.097s at Valencia in 2005 as Rossi Charged From 15th to Third
item.description: A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. Photo: Byron Sullivan / Pexels Marco Melandri beat Nicky Hayden by 0.097 seconds at Valencia 21 years ago today, on November 6, 2005, in the last race of a MotoGP season whose champion had already been settled. Valentino Rossi, who clinched his fifth straight premier-class title at Sepang six weeks earlier, started 15th after a qualifying crash and still finished third. The 2005 Valencia MotoGP finale was a race with nothing on the line for the title, and it still produced one of the closest finishes of the year. A title already decided, a runner-up fight still open Rossi wrapped up the 2005 championship at the Malaysian Grand Prix on September 25, finishing second to Loris Capirossi while his only remaining challenger, Max Biaggi, ended up sixth. It was his fifth consecutive premier-class crown (one in 500cc and four in MotoGP) and his seventh world title overall, according to Crash.net’s race report . That left second place in the standings as the live fight, and it was between two Hondas. Melandri arrived having won in Turkey the race before. He had climbed from 15th in the 2003 standings and 12th in 2004, and another win would secure second place in the championship. Hayden, the Repsol Honda rider, was chasing his best season yet after finishing fifth and eighth in his first two years in the class. What happened at Valencia Fact Detail Date Sunday, November 6, 2005 Event Valencian Community Grand Prix, final round of the 2005 MotoGP season Circuit Circuit Ricardo Tormo, Valencia, Spain MotoGP pole Sete Gibernau (1:31.874) Winner Marco Melandri, Movistar Honda (46:58.152) Margin 0.097s over Nicky Hayden, Repsol Honda Third Valentino Rossi, Yamaha, from 15th on the grid (+2.959s) Attendance 124,520, reported as a sell-out 2005 Valencian Community Grand Prix, MotoGP class. Sources: Crash.net race report; Wikipedia race entry; Road Racing World. Gibernau took pole for the fifth time that season, but his race was over within a few laps with an engine failure. Melandri led from the first corner and Hayden stayed on his tail for the whole 30 laps, on a circuit where overtaking is hard. Melandri opened a small gap, then had a bobble before the final corner that let Hayden close right up. Hayden went for the pass on the exit, and Melandri held his line to take the win. Melandri said afterward it was “a dream come true,” per Road Racing World . A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. He was up five places at the first corner and eighth by the end of lap one, then moved into third on lap six. item.title: ‘The Bad Kinda Nepotism,’ ‘This Is So Lame’ – NBA Fans Enraged By Lakers’ Owner Bob Iger’s Son Will’s Latest Move
item.description: ‘The Bad Kinda Nepotism,’ ‘This Is So Lame’ - NBA Fans Enraged By Lakers’ Owner Bob Iger’s Son Will’s Latest Move The Los Angeles Lakers are waiting on new ownership after former Disney CEO Bob Iger and Josh Kushner agreed in August to buy the franchise. Now Iger’s son is set to call games for the team’s G League affiliate, which opens its first season in the Coachella Valley on Friday night. ESPN’s Dave McMenamin relayed the Coachella Valley Lakers’ announcement Thursday that Will Iger will broadcast the team’s games this season. Fans responded by questioning the family connection. Will Iger Joins Coachella Valley Lakers Broadcasts Alongside A.C. Green Will Iger will handle the play-by-play in 2026-27, with A.C. Green beside him as the analyst. Green, who won three championships with the Lakers, did the same job when the team played as the South Bay Lakers. Will Iger’s first broadcast for the club is the season opener against the Salt Lake City Stars. McMenamin led with the family tie when he passed the team’s news along: “Will Iger, the son of incoming Lakers co-owner Bob Iger, will be broadcasting games for LAL’s G League affiliate this season, the Coachella Valley Lakers announced.” The reaction kept returning to the father-son connection, and the word nepotism came up more than once. Less than 20 minutes after McMenamin’s post, one fan wrote, “This the bad kinda nepotism btw.” Another fan saw the hire as a sign of something broader than one G League broadcast booth: “It’s amazing that we’ve gotten to a spot where people don’t even bother to hide the nepotism anymore. It’s become so normalized.” Will Iger does bring play-by-play experience to the role. Before this hire, he called Austin Spurs games, starting in early 2025 for Spurs Sports & Entertainment on FanDuel Sports Network Southwest, and worked some San Antonio FC home matches as well. That job began more than a year before his father agreed to buy into the Lakers. He has called Indoor Football League games since April. His résumé also includes Columbia and Hofstra athletics, high school games in the Austin area and analyst work on The Bounce, the Dallas Mavericks’ weekly show. Jerry Buss’s 1979 purchase began more than four decades of family ownership, and after he died in 2013, his six children controlled the team through a trust. “For all of the dysfunction of the Buss family, at least they never selected one of the many siblings with a first name that starts with a J to call games,” another fan wrote. item.title: Lions Trade Idea Could Bring Former Starting Cornerback Back to Detroit
item.description: The Detroit Lions are running out of time to strengthen their secondary before the November 10 NFL trade deadline, but one intriguing possibility could bring a familiar face back to the Motor City. And it’s a player Brad Holmes once traded to acquire. Carlton Davis III , who started 13 games for Detroit during the 2024 season before departing in free agency, has surfaced in NFL trade speculation involving the New England Patriots. According to NFL insider Albert Breer, Davis is among the veterans New England could consider moving before Tuesday’s deadline. That creates an interesting hypothetical reunion for a Lions team still searching for dependable outside cornerback help. But would the Patriots actually trade him, and could Detroit afford to bring him back? Jun 10, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III (7) speaks to the media after minicamp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) NFL Insider Identifies Carlton Davis as Possible Trade Candidate During a recent appearance on NBC Sports Boston, Breer discussed New England’s potential willingness to move veteran players as the organization considers its long-term roster construction. As Breer explained while discussing the Patriots’ trade possibilities , Davis could become a candidate because of New England’s desire to get younger and accumulate draft capital. The Patriots have several expensive veterans on their roster, and Breer suggested that moving Davis or defensive tackle Christian Barmore wouldn’t necessarily be surprising. However, there’s an important distinction between the two situations. Breer indicated that New England has had trade conversations involving Barmore, while Davis was identified as someone who could potentially become available. There is no confirmed report that the Lions have contacted New England about Davis or that the Patriots have offered him to Detroit. For now, a reunion remains a hypothetical trade idea rather than a developing negotiation. Carlton Davis Already Knows What It Takes to Play in Detroit The biggest argument for bringing Davis back is simple. The Lions already know exactly what they’re getting. Detroit acquired Davis from Tampa Bay in March 2024, surrendering a third-round draft pick while receiving two sixth-round selections as part of the deal. The veteran immediately became an important part of Detroit’s secondary, starting 13 games and recording 56 tackles, two interceptions, and 11 passes defended before a broken jaw ended his season. His physical coverage style fit what the Lions wanted defensively, and his willingness to challenge opposing receivers made him a valuable presence on the outside. Former Lions cornerback Darius Slay even questioned Detroit’s decision to let Davis leave. item.title: Knueppel Injury Deal Another Blow To Hornets’ NBA Cup Hopes
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are in trouble again. Friday’s NBA Cup game versus the Boston Celtics saw Kon Knueppel ruled out just one day after he finally returned to the court. This news comes straight from the official injury report released Thursday. The second-year sharpshooter played less than six minutes on Wednesday before leaving with a left hamstring strain. Now he sits on the sidelines while the Celtics prepare to visit Spectrum Center. Knueppel’s absence is a disaster for a team already reeling. The 21-year-old missed the first eight games of the season due to the exact same injury. He was supposed to be the spark for an offense that has struggled to find rhythm. Instead, his comeback lasted less than one quarter. Coach Charles Lee offered no timeline for his return after the loss to Brooklyn. “No, I don’t have an update yet,” Lee said afterward, according to Yahoo Sports . A Deep Roster for Boston While Charlotte watches its young star sit, Boston looks ready to roll without its own top guy. Jayson Tatum rested on Wednesday but is expected to play Friday. The Celtics have already proven they can win even when their best player sits out. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night without Tatum. Paul George dropped 25 points and Derrick White added 24 to lead the way. Derrick White stepped up when Payton Pritchard also left the game early with an eye injury. White said his mindset changed when key players went down. “Obviously with JT out and then Payton going out too, I had a little bit more aggressive mind-set,” White said, according to Yahoo Sports . The Celtics believe their depth will carry them through the four-game road trip starting in Charlotte. Hornets Stuck in a Rut Charlotte has lost five games in a row and needs a win badly. They started the season strong with three wins in their first four games but have fallen apart since. The injury to Knueppel makes it nearly impossible to stop Boston’s offense. Brandon Miller struggled mightily on Wednesday, shooting just 2-for-15 from the field. Coach Lee noted that Miller’s defensive effort was still there despite the offensive woes. The Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla praised Paul George’s recent performance. “We need the best version of him for us to be a great team, and I think you were able to see that (Wednesday),” Mazzulla said, according to CBS Sports . Boston enters Friday with a 6-2 record. They are looking to extend their winning streak against a Hornets team that has no answers right now. The loss of Knueppel just confirms what everyone already fears: Charlotte is in deep trouble.

item.title: Alvaro Arbeloa beams as Fulham teenage sensation Josh King earns maiden England call-up from Thomas Tuchel
item.description: Coventry City v Fulham - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has hailed Josh King as the "pride" of the club after the teenage midfielder was handed a shock maiden call-up to the England senior squad. The 19-year-old academy graduate has been selected by Thomas Tuchel for upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain, marking a historic rise for the Craven Cottage starlet. Arbeloa hails Fulham’s rising star Arbeloa could not hide his delight after watching one of his brightest talents reach the international stage. The former Real Madrid defender turned manager spoke glowingly of the teenager, who has become the first Fulham outfield player to be selected for the Three Lions since Bobby Zamora. The call-up represents a massive milestone for a player who has spent more than a decade developing within the club's youth system. "This is a special moment for him, for us as a club and obviously for our supporters. I think Josh is the pride of our club and our supporters. He came to this club when he was eight years old. And now, when you look at him, how he’s playing, how he’s performing, we are really proud of him. So I think it’s a big step for him. I’m so happy for him because he’s a very humble kid," Arbeloa told Sky Sports . High praise paired with a reality check The Fulham boss believes this is only the beginning for the versatile midfielder, who has already travelled with the senior national team previously without making an appearance. Yet despite beaming with pride over his role in nurturing one of the club's brightest prospects, Arbeloa was quick to sound a vital note of caution, urging the rising star to keep his feet firmly planted on the ground. "You can see every day he wants to improve, he wants to work, he wants to become a better player every day. So I think it’s a special day for him and for all of us. I think he’s on the way to become a star; a very, very important player in this world. I’m so happy that I coached him, helped him to develop and reach his level. But he needs to stay humble like he is," Arbeloa noted. Tuchel explains the shock selection Tuchel has clearly been impressed by more than just the technical ability shown by the 19-year-old during his breakthrough season. The German tactician, who is preparing his side for high-stakes Nations League matches, suggested that King’s character played a pivotal role in his inclusion. While the squad features established stars, Tuchel is keen to reward those showing the right mentality in training and domestic competition. "He is just a fantastic character. item.title: Sam Mewis makes her picks for 2026 NWSL champion, MVP
item.description: The NWSL playoffs begin this weekend with four quarterfinal matchups: San Diego Wave vs. Utah Royals (Friday, Nov. 6), Kansas City Current vs. Angel City FC (Saturday, Nov. 7), Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign (Sunday, Nov. 8) and Washington Spirit vs. Portland Thorns (Sunday, Nov. 8). Former U.S. women's national team star Sam Mewis, who hosts “The Women’s Game” podcast for the Men In Blazers network, said there’s one particular match she has circled on her calendar. “Kansas City versus Angel City, I had that circled the second that seeding got finalized,” Mewis told USA TODAY Sports in an interview on Nov. 5. “I feel that both teams are actually in really great form coming into playoffs. Among the top teams, I wouldn't want to play against either team. A few of us were saying it's kind of a bummer that this is a first-round game because it feels like a really big one.” Fourth-seeded Kansas City will host the quarterfinal at CPKC Stadium, where the Current have a 32-match regular-season unbeaten streak dating back to July 6, 2024. The magic might not extend to the playoffs, though; the Current lost at home in the 2025 quarterfinals to eventual champion Gotham. Fifth-seeded Angel City , meanwhile, has been on a tear since firing head coach Alexander Straus in June. Days after the coaching change, Angel City also made a mid-season trade with Kansas City to acquire attacker Ally Sentnor, who will face off against her former club in the quarterfinal. Under interim coach Leif Gunnar Smerud, Angel City went undefeated in its final 10 regular-season matches. “There's that expression, the 'new manager bump,’” Mewis said. “Things that were stagnant or not working, players suddenly feel the freedom to do things a little bit differently or respond in a way that they maybe weren't supposed to before. But I think what we're seeing with Angel City is actually really unique, and it feels like everything has come together recently.” Mewis, a three-time NWSL champion with the Western New York Flash and North Carolina Courage, said momentum is an important factor in the postseason. That could be results-based momentum, like San Diego going undefeated in its last seven games and locking up the No. 2 seed. Or it could be emotional momentum, like Seattle playing in honor of captain Jess Fishlock, who plans to retire at the end of the season. As volatile as the playoffs can be, Mewis is predicting that the top two seeded teams will reach the NWSL title game: defending champions and 2026 NWSL Shield winners Gotham FC — whose roster includes Mewis’ sister-in-law Sam Kerr and several USWNT players — and the San Diego Wave. item.title: As LIV Golf burned through cash, a lot of people made a lot of money
item.description: LIV Golf is shutting down after the investment firm that considered giving it $300 million withdrew its offer, forcing the league to begin liquidating its assets. LIV attorney Matthew Williams confirmed Thursday in New Jersey Bankruptcy Court the league will start selling its assets Monday after BC Partners decided it would not invest in LIV 2.0. Why did LIV Golf fail? Inside the nearly $6 billion experiment gone wrong The beginning of the end for the league created by Greg Norman as a competitor to the PGA Tour was when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund decided in April it could not continue to bankroll a business that offered nothing in return. And it took burning more than $5 billion for the PIF to realize that. Since then, golfers surely tired of CEO Scott O'Neil's outrageous claims and promises, all the while making sure he was taken care of as the ship was sinking. One by one, LIV's biggest assets — its players — bailed. Jumping into a future of uncertainty after being part of the money grab. All the while, O'Neil kept up the charade. After PIF pulled the plug seven months ago, O'Neil said LIV would do "what we do best: putting on the most compelling show in sports." One month ago, he said he believed deeply in the future of LIV and would build something distinctive alongside their players. "We’re delivering on our major milestones," he said. Social media reacts: Here's what people are saying about LIV Golf's demise LIV and BC Partners were seeking 30 to 40 players to compete next season. The Financial Times reported Wednesday about 30 players were currently committed and about 10 were undecided. Marquee names such as Brooks Koepka, Patrick Reed, Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton had departed (Koepka and Reed started the trend early this year). Others such as Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Dustin Johnson were among 19 players whose contracts were allowed to be rejected amid bankruptcy and the restructuring process. DeChambeau appeared to be the last holdout, saying on a podcast Oct. 2 he believed LIV 2.0 can make "full financial sense” and hoped it would last forever. LIV indicated it had between $100 million and $500 million in assets and $500 million to $1 billion in liabilities. Lawsuits were piling up from contractors and vendors owed more than $4 million for work this year. That list included Fresh Tape Media, which produced LIV's preseason media days in January held at the Palm Beach County Convention Center. Additionally, 27 players were stiffed out of a combined $64.2 million. O’Neil, though, received more than $13.6 million in payroll, bonuses, benefits, retention payments and expense reimbursements from Sept. 2025 through Aug. 2026. LIV filed for bankruptcy Sept. 8. item.description: Ex-Gunner reflects on Arsenal spell ahead of Emirates return with Hull Hull City’s Brooke Norton-Cuffy has reflected positively on his time with Arsenal, but he’ll be playing to win with his new side on Saturday. Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images Former Arsenal academy youngster Brooke Norton-Cuffy returned to England to play in the Premier League this summer, joining Hull City from Genoa . The move was a positive one from an Arsenal perspective, allowing them to cash in on the sell-on clause in Norton-Cuffy’s contract. The Gunners reportedly netted around £2.4m from the deal. But the downside is obviously that Arsenal will now have to play against Norton-Cuffy, with the 22-year-old set to make his first appearance against his old club in their Premier League clash on Saturday. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images Speaking ahead of the game, Norton-Cuffy insisted he still has many positive memories of his time in north London, although he’ll be returning to the Emirates Stadium looking for three points for Hull. “I look back at my time at Arsenal with fond memor­ies,” Norton-Cuffy said . “I learned a lot. Rather than integrating the right-back with the senior side, Arsenal opted to send him out on various loans to Lincoln City , Rotherham United , Coventry City , and Millwall . item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - MARCH 29: Beau Ankeney (35) Grand Canyon Infielder takes a big swing during a baseball game between the Arizona Wildcats and the Grand Canyon Lopes on March 29, 2022, at GCU Ballpark in Phoenix, AZ. (Photo by Zac BonDurant/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There are two particular categories of player that go under the radar in the major league amateur draft each year. The first are college seniors. If you didn’t get drafted by your junior year or earlier, as a JUCO or prep player, there’s a natural stigma attached. The second are first basemen. Because the position is usually filled by less athletic players whose value is heavily tied up in their bat, only the top ranked college first baseman really get much notice, and they tend to go in the early rounds as some of the better hitters each year. Leaving aside the player and just considering the profile, Spencer Torkelson was a hard player to philosophically wrap one’s head around as the first overall pick in the draft back in 2020. Living up to that would’ve required him to develop quickly into one of the better hitters in baseball. There’s a reason you very rarely see a 1-1 first baseman. Detroit Tigers prospect Beau Ankeney checks both boxes, and he definitely didn’t get much attention on draft day 2025 when they picked him in the 14th round out of Loyola Marymount and paid him just the minimum signing bonus. He played three years at Grand Canyon University before breaking out and transferring to Loyola for his senior season in 2025. That was notable, as he was clearly a bit of a late bloomer. Also notable was his muscular six-foot-three, 235 pound frame. He only played in four games after the draft, so there wasn’t anything to get excited about yet. That changed in 2026. Ankeney mashed 24 home runs total, including 9 in just 27 games at the High-A level after he was promoted in late July. He took his walks. He showed pretty good athleticism for a first baseman, with enough speed to handle a corner outfield spot here and there. His raw power really stood out, as he averaged 92 mph off the bat, which is great even at the MLB level, and maxed out at 114.4 mph off the bat, giving him a 65 FV grade on his raw power potential. There are still five months left on the schedule, with back-to-backs and spells of three-games-in-four-nights filling in the calendar. Most teams can get off to a bad start and still be just fine. Just over two weeks into the season, it already feels like there are six teams who are already toast. Some of these teams knew they would be bad coming into the year, while others dreamed of breaking into the playoffs. The unfortunate reality for these teams is they can’t even count on a high draft pick next year anymore after the league’s anti-tanking lottery reform was put in place this season ahead of the 2027 draft. item.title: The Denver Broncos Coaches Who Built the Standard a Mile High
item.description: “Thanks, Dan, for giving me an opportunity in the NFL.” – A (hopefully) future Hall of Fame coach On Thursday, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced five coaching candidates still in contention for its Class of 2027. Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves, and Mike Shanahan. Five men who have collectively made an awful lot of football fans very happy or wholly infuriated. For Broncos fans, two of those names brought a lot of joy and carry a particular bit of weight. And while only one of the five will advance to the final round of consideration later this month, it’s worth spending a little time appreciating just how much those two men gave to a franchise that has spent much of the last half-century expecting to be amongst the best in football. Because those expectations didn’t come from nowhere. I was a young kid when the Broncos made their first Super Bowl appearance in January 1978. My family had moved to California a few years earlier, and I remember feeling very far away from Colorado, perhaps for the first time. I’d gotten Lyle Alzado’s signature while I was home visiting my dad at Summer Camp in 1977, at the beginning of that huge year, and there was something about watching Red Miller, Craig Morton, and that remarkable Orange Crush defense representing the place I still thought of as home that made those miles feel a little longer. Maybe a lot longer. The Broncos lost to Dallas that day, 27-10. It was a tough introduction to the particular heartbreak of being a Denver football fan, though we’d eventually become pretty damned proficient at that particular exercise. But Red Miller had done something extraordinary. He’d taken a franchise that had never even reached the playoffs to 12-2, and brought it all the way to the Super Bowl. He’d shown us what was possible. Dan Reeves was the man who made us believe that possibility could happen again. And again. And again. I’d just moved home to Colorado when Reeves arrived in Denver in 1981, a 37-year-old former Dallas Cowboys player and assistant who had already experienced championship football from both sides of the sideline. Within a few years, he’d helped bring John Elway to Denver, and the two began one of the most successful, occasionally contentious partnerships in Broncos history. Over 12 seasons, Reeves won 110 regular-season games, five division titles, and three AFC championships. His teams reached the playoffs six times and suffered only two losing seasons. item.title: ‘They killed James Harden for it’: Doc Rivers says nobody talked about what Luka Doncic kept on doing
item.description: Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images Luka Doncic and James Harden share a similar playing style. The Los Angeles Lakers and Cleveland Cavaliers stars share a heliocentric, high-usage and step-back-heavy style, and that makes them both brilliant. However, Doc Rivers, who coached Harden and watched his team play against Doncic, has claimed that the two players are actually very different. But they did share one similarity for which only Harden was criticised, says Rivers. Doc Rivers says Luka Doncic got away with holding the ball but James Harden didn’t Rivers coached Harden with the Philadelphia 76ers between 2022 and 2023. Despite the obvious similarities everyone talks about, the 65-year-old claimed that they are not alike at all – except for the fact that they both hold onto the ball ‘forever’. Rivers claimed that Harden was blasted for doing it, but Doncic constantly got away with it, even though he did it a lot more. On his podcast , when Ben Simmons spoke about Harden and Doncic’s similar heliocentric style of play, Rivers replied: “He’s different. They are different. Even though they both hold the ball forever. “Even in Luka’s heyday in Dallas, people never talked about it, but they killed James Harden for having the ball, but Luka actually had the ball more in his hands, and no one ever said that, which is really interesting. “It is different. They are similar in the way they hold the ball. It feels like Luka does the action quicker than James. They both are extraordinary passers.” Harden was definitely criticised, but Doncic didn’t completely get away with it. Both players got their share of stick from fans, pundits and the media for holding on to the ball. Now, Doncic plays for the Lakers and Harden for the Cavaliers, and both players have evolved their games compared to a few years ago. Neither is as heliocentric as they were in the past. item.title: Arsenal could make January move for Juventus star
item.description: Arsenal could make January move for Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has emerged as one of the most exciting attacking talents in European football, with the Turkish youngster becoming a central figure at Juventus. However, his impressive development has also attracted interest from Arsenal , who would love to bring him to the Emirates Stadium. Yildiz came through the youth ranks at Bayern Munich before Juventus secured his services and offered him a pathway into their first team. That decision has proved successful, with the attacker developing into one of the most influential players in the Italian side’s squad. His performances have caught Arsenal’s attention, and the Gunners have reportedly monitored him for some time. His ability to operate on the left wing and make an impact in attack makes him an appealing option as they consider ways to strengthen their forward line. Arsenal continue to monitor Juventus star Yildiz has been on Arsenal’s transfer list over the last two seasons, but Juventus have shown little willingness to let him leave . The Italian club consider him one of their most important players and are determined to keep him in Turin. Nevertheless, Arsenal will know that even highly valued players can become available if the right offer arrives. Juventus may be reluctant to sell, but a sufficiently attractive proposal could test their resolve. The bigger question is whether the Italian side would even consider losing such an important player halfway through the season. Arsenal are currently looking at attacking reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window, making the timing of any potential approach particularly significant. Kenan Yildiz (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Yildiz among Arsenal’s January targets According to Mirror Football , Yildiz is one of the players Arsenal would like to add to their squad when the transfer window reopens in the new year. The report underlines the Gunners’ interest in strengthening their attacking options, although convincing Juventus to negotiate could prove difficult.
